newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Motors to raise GDI engine output.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Motors to raise GDI engine output.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Monday it would increase production of GDI (Gasoline Direct Injection) engines to 33,200 units by the end of March 1997 due to strong domestic demand.
In October, Mitsubishi raised its production plan for the engines to 26,000 units from an initially planned 18,000.
The GDI engine is used in the Mitsubishi Galant sedan and Legnum station wagon which were launched in Japan on August 29 with a combined monthly sales target of 7,000.
Cumulative domestic orders for the models reached 36,000 units as of the end of November, comprising 16,000 Galants and 20,000 Legnums, a Mitsubishi spokesman said.
Mitsubishi said its GDI engine consumes up to 35 percent less fuel than its predecessor and emits up to 35 percent less carbon dioxide.

Mitsubishi produces GDI engines at its Kyoto plant. The spokesman said the firm would increase the number of temporary workers at the plant to 640 in December, and to 680 in January, compared with 570 in November.
